revision_summary:
Two timestamp/quote misattributions must be fixed: (1) bill_document_audit.result_quote at 02:52 currently shows the rep's later scheduling line ('I mean, I could look now...') — that text belongs to the rep at ~06:03-06:09; the actual customer line at 02:52 is 'Yeah. It might not be for a little while. She just opened her own, retail business, but she's over there right now.' Replace or move accordingly. (2) script_coverage 'appointment_set' customer_quote 'If you got a Friday morning, that would be pretty ideal' is mistimed at 06:03 — that ts is the rep speaking; the customer's line actually occurs around 06:27-06:31. Correct both timestamps.

Also: reclassify cherry_pick_moments[0] from protocols.spouse_decision to verify.title_co_owners — no spouse-objection trigger phrase occurred; the rep proactively surfaced co-ownership during verify and simply didn't follow through to confirm her presence at the in-person visit, which is a different (softer) gap than the schema's spouse_decision protocol (which addresses customers pushing back with 'I need to talk to my spouse'). Adjust the trajectory_verdict and coaching_focus language that treats this as equivalent to the SESSION20-style spousal-exclusion failure — the in-person visit format means the wife's absence is not confirmed, only unconfirmed, and the current wording ('no attempt to get her on the line or appointment') should be softened to reflect that this is a home visit, not a phone appointment requiring active coordination.

Trim the speculative coaching angle at cherry_pick_moments[3] (03:38) tying business ownership/family size to usage/bill size — this isn't grounded in schema or transcript evidence and reads as invented sales theory; either cut it or reframe strictly as a missed rapport-to-qualification bridge without the income/usage inference.

Soften trajectory_verdict tone slightly ('structurally incomplete') to match the actual severity — a locked day/time with an unconfirmed but not contradicted co-owner attendance is a moderate gap, not a structural failure.
